utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, The Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, counsel. Mark Harmon, Salvatore Cannata, Barney Thomas, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Harmon. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. Mr. Perisic is today represented by Tina Drolec; Milos Androvic, Chad Mair, our legal assistants; as well as Colleen Rohan, our consultant; and Daniela Tasic, our case manager; as well as Gregor Guy-Smith; and Novak Lukic as counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Harmon, I guess the Prosecution wanted to raise something with the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Two items. Mr. Thomas is here so he can make some submissions to the Trial Chamber before we begin with the witness. So in order I'd like to have Mr. Thomas proceed first. Second of all, Your Honour in reflecting on what happened on Monday in efforts to streamline the procedures that we have here. First of all, I can report that we have -- counsel, my colleagues from the Defence and have I met. We have reached a number of agreements. Those discussions are ongoing. We have submitted a large number of schedules from the master, the Randall master list to the Defence to see if we can reach agreement, and we intend to have additional discussions today on those -- on those lists that we have submitted. One thing that was particularly difficult in terms of the procedures was what I have attempted to do is to identify some exemplars of documents and then thematically there are a number of documents that fit the same theme in court. Monday I was reading out those numbers with some degree of success and some degree of a lack of success, but I was reading them out. And in order to be more efficient what I propose to Your Honours is the following: When we come to the long schedules of documents that are in similar theme, we have prepared lists of those documents. I've shown those lists -- or counsel is aware of those lists. We have itemised by 65 ter number. The item that would be on the list with -- essentially a short description similar to what is in the master list, the ERNs and the source. And rather than me reading them out what I propose, if the Court is agreeable, is that I would submit the list to the Court and counsel. It would be given a number, an exhibit number. I would then show it to the witness, ask the witness to review it, ask the witness to affirm the contents of it, and then I would ask that the documents identified on the list be marked as exhibits. It has the benefit of being -- I think faster and more efficient, at least, as a benefit of identifying for the Registrar specifically the items and -- that's one proposal. The alternative proposal, Your Honours, is for me to continue in the way in which I did on Monday, which is read the numbers one by one into the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which is what we are trying to avoid.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is what I am trying to avoid, Your Honour. That is the proposal that I have, and I leave it to Your Honours. I could submit Your Honours now and a copy to counsel, a copy of the schedule, a sample schedule. The Court could review it, and -- if the Court wishes at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're happy to do that, Mr. Harmon. Do you want to do that right away?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, I leave to Your Honours. I'm in your hands, Your Honour. I have prepared a number of these if Your Honours want to see them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure, we can have a look at them right away and tell you whether -- the proposal is not very clear in my mind so my -- our comments might not be as intelligent as you have conceived them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, I apologise, Your Honour. If this could be distributed to Your Honours and to counsel. What Your Honours have before you is a document that relates to a theme. In this case it is maintenance by the VJ. What I intend to do is call forth on the screen, in this case, two exemplars. I don't want to call up the items on this schedule because otherwise we will be here forever. These items have, in fact, been agreed to by the Defence. This was part of our discussions yesterday. So what I propose to do is show Your Honours and counsel the two exemplars on this theme, and then I would ask that this be marked as an exhibit, and then I would show this to the witness, ask the witness to look at it and affirm that it's accurate, in terms of the sources. And then this would be an exhibit. The Court would have -- and counsel would know which of the items now have been either accepted or if there are objections which ones for which there are objections. That is my proposal Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Once the witness has seen that, it would mean that this whole list is then admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct. And in some cases, Your Honour, because we have, as you know from looking at the master list, we have shaded areas. They're protected. In some situations the list may contain shaded areas in which case we would request that the list itself be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. That would be no problem. Let's just get confirmation -- or are you still on your feet. I see Mr. Guy-Smith is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll defer to Mr. Guy-Smith. I have some more to discuss, but I will defer on there topic and then I'll go into something else, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As we view it, and we do confirm what Mr. Harmon has said thus far, it seems to us that what we are in effect doing is what I would call a modified J of the guidelines that we have in this case. That would be a modified tendering of evidence from the bar table, and it would be J subparagraph 23. We're really dealing with the same kind of thing. We have a list. Each exhibit has a description. It is clear from the exhibits that are on here -- the example he has given what the relevance may be. Obviously, if there is an relevance issue that will be described and we are in a position where there's a joint agreement with regard to having these exhibits coming in this fashion and any objections that we might have -- our objections by virtue of the way doing it right now would be noted for the moment orally although we will at some point file -- probably in the hopes of this week if not early next week a global objection to any concern we have, which deals not with the specific issues that have presented themselves thus far. I think we're working along the same lines. Absolutely. And I hope that what I said did not seem to change that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, I hear you Mr. Guy-Smith. The only difference is that from what I was thinking of between me and what you are both suggesting is I thought you were going to be working through documents that you think can go in and say, Look, we have no objection to this. They can go in, throw them in en masse, but these we object to and can we go through them in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We're very close to being able to do that too. I think this first round, there are still some legal issues that may revolve some of the documents, but those legal issues are legal issues that are distinct from the normal kinds of admissibility, battles that we might have here with regard to foundation issues or authentication issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll see how you go about it as we go along. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We think we have a positive -- we really do think we have a positive approach to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The second thing I observed on Monday and taking Your Honours' comments into consideration, one thing Your Honour said, you said, Your Honour, was that you were concerned we were going too fast, and you didn't know what was being admitted. Now, when -- there are two solutions to that. The first solution is I can slow down on the screen. We can ask that the images on the screen stay there a bit longer, and that's one solution. Another solution would be to submit paper copies to Your Honours and would you have them before you, and you could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me intervene right there. If you are going to come up with an expedited manner of tendering documents like we have either suggested or like I was saying. There is no need for that. Because then we will -- as I said -- we'll spend the time reading the exhibits once they're in the office. My comment related to the point where you were putting them one by one, but we just didn't see the content of what was being admitted, and I said what is the point of seeing them if we can't see the content. But if you throw them in en masse and we can sit in the office and read them, that's a different story.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So that I don't have to see them on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Finally, if we follow the procedures that he did on Monday, I have some additional binders that I would like to present to the witness before commencing his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we call the witness, the Chamber has a minor administrative issue to raise with the parties. The parties have filed a joint request for waiver of confidentiality for a witness who is supposed to come fairly early in the new week. Obviously -- the decision has been granted, signed this morning. That request has been granted. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. You may call the witness, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, one brief matter before I call the witness, and that is a housekeeping matter. When we broke the last time, there was a disagreement in respect of Exhibit 65 ter number 8787.13. That has been resolved. The parties agree that that can be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does the Defence confirm?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Registrar can you please give an exhibit number to that exhibit. It will be Exhibit 65 ter 8787.13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, am I right to ask the Registrar to assign an exhibit number to that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- document? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit P844.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I give Mr. Randall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just greet Mr. Randall before you give him that. Good Morning, Mr. Randall.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good. Just to remind you, Mr. Randall, that you are you still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony on Monday to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Mr. Harmon. And just to say sorry to call you a couple of minutes before we asked to go for break, but that's the way things go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You don't have to apologise. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have a series of binders, Your Honour. We'll be covering these topics, and I ask that they be presented to Mr. Randall.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Randall, if you can avail, Your Honour, to the first binder, which is the thin binder, unused annual leave. It says on the spine of the binder.

utterances.speaker: BRETTON RANDALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I've got that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If can he can go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 8088 on the monitor, please. And that's found, Your Honours, on the master list at page 177 of the master list. If the English version could be centred that would be fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Randall, can you identify this item that's before you?

utterances.speaker: BRETTON RANDALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a decision issued by Colonel Milan Biga of the 30th Personnel Centre, in respect of person by the name of Bozo Novak. In request of compensation for unused annual leave. It was received from the government of the Republic of Serbia in response to Request for Assistance 1560.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And who is Mr. Biga?

utterances.speaker: BRETTON RANDALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was at one stage the officer in charge of the Yugoslav army, 30th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that that be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to be clear, we have a document in front of us that the Defence and the Prosecution did not discuss. We have an objection to this document. Can we please look at page 2, Your Honours? There will be a general objection here from the Defence, because Mr. Harmon, as far as I know, has a number of documents that he would like to tender in this form. This document was drafted significantly after the indictment period. It's some time from 2007, I think, and discussions the retro active recognition of certain status rights. There are a number of these documents. The Defence believes that this document, which was adopted beyond the indictment period, generally is not relevant for the facts that are the subject of the indictment; so we are stating a general objection to the relevancy of documents of this nature, not the authenticity of them. I am being told by my assistants now that the document has no date. But I believe that Mr. Harmon and I agree that all of these documents which were signed by Mr. Biga were drafted or adopted from 2000 -- actually from 1999, 2000, and 2001. That is the period, and I believe that Mr. Randall can confirm this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the last dates that you are giving now at page 30, lines 14, you say 1999, 2000, and 2001; however, at page 30, line 4, you said this document is as recent as 2007. Which is which?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a mistake in the transcript, I assume it is due to my speed. On page 30 line 4 I said from 2007 [as interpreted], actually, so that's where the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 2000 and that's where the error lies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Lukic. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you like me to address the relevancy objection? There may be additional relevance objections, but I will be glad to address there one now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... the objection as raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, please. Your Honour, this, first of all, I think the date is irrelevant when this decision was reached. This decision and the subsequent decisions that you will see resolved significant issues identifying the status of the people who are the subject of this litigation. Ultimately concluding and, in fact, it being not disputed that the people who were the litigants in this case were members of the VJ who were sent out of Serbia and the FRY on orders of a superior officer. That's one of the contests issues in this case, Your Honour. What is the status of the persons in the 30th Personnel Centre. What we will be presenting this morning are decisions in which a domestic Court based on complaints made by VJ soldiers who served in the 30th Personnel Centre resolved their complaints, resolved their claims and found that they were members of the VJ who had been sent out of Serbia, members of the 30th Personnel Centre and members of the 40th Personnel Centre had been sent out of the FRY on orders of a superior officer; and that is one of the central issues in this case, and will you see, as we will be presenting a series of judgements in which that issue was addressed in the FRY. So that's our response. That's my response, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could that be given an exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P845.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 8087 on the screen. That is found also at page 177 of the master list, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Randall, can you identify this document, please.

utterances.speaker: BRETTON RANDALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a Yugoslav army supreme military court judgement deciding in the complaint filed by Bozo Novak. It's dated 22 February 2001. It was received from the government of the Republic of Serbia in response to Request for Assistance 1560.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we -- could that be given an exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document is admitted -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, because the objection was overruled in the last instances to the extended documents that are being admitted fall the same category right, which are judgements that are outside of the indictment period and deal with this particular time-frame issue. Could we have a continuing objection rather than jumping up each and every time and breaking the flow of this, and Mr. Harmon would be so kind as to tell us when he is shifting to another kind of document, in case we have other objections, we appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber will note that are you a global objection, which is globally overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, both this item and the previous item should be under seal because they're protected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Registrar, and an exhibit number under seal, and please place P845 under seal as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P846, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We can go back into public session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session. On that note -- sorry, go ahead Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry for the interruption, Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would that be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, it would be, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honours is found on page 197 of the master list, and if I could have 8743 put on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Randall, can you identify this particular document?

utterances.speaker: BRETTON RANDALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a judgement issued by the Yugoslav army supreme military court dated 29 January 2001, in respect of a complaint filed by Colonel Zarko Ljubovojevic in respect of compensation for unused annual leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And is there a number on this judgement?

utterances.speaker: BRETTON RANDALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Supreme military court 1694/200.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And what is the source of this document, Mr. Randall?

utterances.speaker: BRETTON RANDALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was provided by the government of the Republic of Serbia in response to Request for Assistance 1537.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could that be given an exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It may be. Under seal, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, this is a public document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit P847.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether or not we've moved to a different kind of document or not, and it's for that reason that I rise. If we have -- we if re in the same class of document, then obviously the continuing objections stands; and I also would comment on the fact that, as I'm reading the document, this document is apparently an administrative decision so with regard to the basis for this judgement and the evidentiary standards that you were used, there is no knowledge whatsoever, which may well go to an issue of the weight, if any, that is given to the relevance of this document as opposed to its admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand what you are saying, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Surely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what are you asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm reiterating the relevancy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought we were agreed that have you had made a global objection which was globally overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct. But as I was looking at this document I saw something that struck something else in my mind. So I was commenting on that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you saying this is an exception to the global ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No -- I'm not sure because I don't know from Mr. Harmon whether or not we are in a new set of documents or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know what you're asking for and what I can do to rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm making the same ruling -- I don't make ruling obviously. I'm making the same objection that I made before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I though we had agreed that you are not going to be standing up because we've dealt with that objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct, but I'm not sure whether this is a different class or the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then you can't be making the same objection that you made before. It must be a new objection and you got to tell me what the ground is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might ask, Mr. Harmon, if this is the same type of document as we're dealing with before, I will know whether or not I should stand or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I can respond, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is similar to the previous exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Then is there no reason for me to be standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The next exhibit is found on page 217 of the master list. If 9191 could be put on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Randall, can you identify the exhibit that is before you?

utterances.speaker: BRETTON RANDALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a judgement issued by the federal court in Belgrade, in relation to an appeal of Zdravko Dokmanovic. The number is 156/98.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the provenance of this document?

utterances.speaker: BRETTON RANDALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was provided by the government of the Republic of Serbia, in response to Request for Assistance 1664.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could that be given an exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P848, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honours, is found at page 155 of the master list. Could I have Exhibit 7925 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Randall, can you identify the exhibit that is before you?

utterances.speaker: BRETTON RANDALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision issued by the military post 3001, dated 17 May 2001, in respect of Colonel General Ratko Mladic, in respect of compensation for unused annual leave for the years 1991 to 1995, inclusive, under the name issued by Colonel Milan Biga. And than was received from the government of Serbia and Montenegro in response to Request for Assistance 1127-B.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Could that be given an exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, it may. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P849, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have Exhibit 8394 on the monitor, please, and that is found at page 190 of the master list.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Randall, can you identify 8394, the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BRETTON RANDALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a decision issued by the Yugoslav army military post 1790, Belgrade, dated 10 October 2002. It's a decision concerning retired Major-General Milan Celeketic, regarding entitlements to salary and special payments for unused annual leave, for the years 1992, 1993, 1994, bearing the signature -- bearing the name of Colonel Slobodan Tadic and that was received from the government of the Republic of Serbia, in response to Request for Assistance 1560.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could that be admitted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P850, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
